title: QCHAP agent output (q-chapter-picker) -- the chapter ONE question belongs to
description: ITEM GRANULARITY: one question. THE CHAPTER LIST IS CLOSED: `chapter_codes` must be codes from the list the runner supplied, drawn from the product's own ExamChapterTopicMappings taxonomy (114 chapters, 1,242 topics), or ["unsure"]. A chapter the agent composes is a chapter the product cannot show. A chapter plainly missing from the list is a FINDING -- answer unsure and name what was expected in `note` -- because a taxonomy gap reported once gets fixed, while a question forced into the nearest chapter is wrong forever and looks right. Two codes are allowed only where the question genuinely needs both; a word appearing in passing is not a second chapter.

chapter_codes.description: `chapter_code` values from the supplied list (e.g. PHYNEETENGWOP), or exactly ["unsure"]. Validated against the list in scripts/checks/QCHAP.py -- the check owns no chapter list of its own, it reads the one the item carried.

chapter_names.description: Copied from the list for readability. `chapter_codes` are what count.

why.description: One sentence naming the fact the CORRECT ANSWER depends on -- not what the stem mentions. A question whose stem describes a circuit but whose answer turns on Ohm's law belongs to the chapter that teaches Ohm's law.

proposed_chapter.description: The chapter you wanted and could not find, named as it should appear in the taxonomy (for example "Transport in Plants", or "Doppler Effect"). Fill this WHENEVER you answer unsure, pick "Unspecified Topic", or settle for a near neighbour you are not happy with. It is how a gap becomes a fix: scripts/collect_taxonomy_gaps.py gathers these into one list with the questions that wanted each, so a missing chapter is added once rather than worked around for ever.
